question: A
title: Affordable Housing
explanation: Authorizes Baltimore City to borrow up to $22 million for affordable housing and related property acquisition, rehabilitation, construction, assistance, and improvements.
if_for: The city may borrow the authorized amount for the specified purposes. Authorization alone does not establish which projects receive funding or when money is spent.
if_against: This question would not authorize the proposed borrowing.

question: B
title: School Facilities
explanation: Authorizes Baltimore City to borrow up to $60 million for school buildings, equipment, athletic facilities, and related community health and recreation facilities.
if_for: The city may borrow the authorized amount for the specified facilities and related costs.
if_against: This question would not authorize the proposed borrowing.

question: C
title: Community And Economic Development
explanation: Authorizes Baltimore City to borrow up to $50 million for its economic development program, including neighborhood improvements, blight reduction, housing assistance, business support, and other eligible projects.
if_for: The city may borrow the authorized amount and use it for the purposes described in the question, including eligible loans and grants.
if_against: This question would not authorize the proposed borrowing.

question: D
title: Public Infrastructure
explanation: Authorizes Baltimore City to borrow up to $148 million for public infrastructure, including city buildings, libraries, parks, streets, utilities, technology, and related improvements.
if_for: The city may borrow the authorized amount for eligible infrastructure and related costs.
if_against: This question would not authorize the proposed borrowing.

question: E
title: Contract Bidding And Awards
explanation: Removes charter provisions requiring lowest-bid awards, governing tied bids, and specifying certain bid and performance bonds. Those subjects could instead be governed through ordinances or regulations.
if_for: The charter provisions would be removed on November 7, 2028, unless a relevant ordinance or regulation takes effect sooner.
if_against: The existing charter provisions on contract bidding and awards remain.

question: F
title: Budget Process And Board Of Estimates
explanation: Changes legislative deadlines and the budget process, transfers financial responsibilities from the Board of Estimates to other city officials or bodies, removes the preliminary budget hearing process, and removes the charter’s $1 million emergency contingency-fund cap.
if_for: The changes take effect on different dates: December 3, 2026 for most changes, December 5, 2028 for legislative approval and veto changes, and November 7, 2028 for removed sections unless replaced sooner.
if_against: The existing charter provisions governing legislation, the budget, and the Board of Estimates remain.

question: G
title: Franchises And Minor Privileges
explanation: Protects the city’s stormwater system from sale or franchise rental, clarifies that conduit space may be rented while the conduit system cannot be sold, and revises permissions for certain uses of city property.
if_for: An executive agency could grant minor privileges under a process established by ordinance. Most changes take effect December 3, 2026; removed sections take effect November 7, 2028 unless replaced sooner.
if_against: The existing charter provisions on franchises and minor privileges remain.

question: H
title: Department Of Water And Wastewater
explanation: Creates a separate Department of Water and Wastewater, transferring water and wastewater responsibilities from Public Works. It also removes the charter requirement that Public Works bureaus be established or abolished by ordinance.
if_for: The charter changes take effect January 1, 2029.
if_against: The existing charter provisions governing water and wastewater systems remain.

question: I
title: Baltimore Baby Fund
explanation: Creates a separate fund to support the economic stability of Baltimore families with newborns. It requires an annual city contribution tied to taxable property value and allows grants and donations.
if_for: The city must contribute an amount equivalent to $0.03 per $100 of taxable property value annually. Fund money cannot replace existing newborn funding or be transferred to unrelated purposes.
if_against: The proposed fund would not be established by this amendment.

question: A
title: Affordable Housing Loan
explanation: Whether to let the city borrow up to $20 million for affordable housing, including acquiring property, housing assistance, rehabilitation, development, and support for the Affordable Housing Trust Fund.
if_for: Authorize this borrowing for the listed purposes. Approval does not establish that bonds were issued or money was spent.
if_against: Do not authorize this borrowing through this measure; rejection would not itself end existing housing programs.

question: B
title: School Loan
explanation: Whether to let the city borrow up to $55 million for school property, buildings, athletic and auxiliary facilities, improvements, reconstruction, and equipment.
if_for: Authorize this borrowing for the listed school capital purposes. Approval does not establish that bonds were issued or projects were funded or completed.
if_against: Do not authorize this borrowing through this measure; rejection would not itself eliminate other school funding.

question: C
title: Community And Economic Development Loan
explanation: Whether to let the city borrow up to $50 million for neighborhood and economic development, including property redevelopment, business and job programs, homeownership and home repairs, cultural projects, and tourism.
if_for: Authorize this borrowing and the listed uses, including eligible loans and grants. Approval does not establish that bonds were issued or money was allocated or spent.
if_against: Do not authorize this borrowing through this measure; rejection would not itself end other development programs.

question: D
title: Public Infrastructure
explanation: Whether to let the city borrow up to $125 million for public infrastructure, including streets, bridges, city facilities, libraries, parks, recreation facilities, information technology, and trees.
if_for: Authorize this borrowing for the listed capital purposes. Approval does not establish that bonds were issued or particular projects were funded or completed.
if_against: Do not authorize this borrowing through this measure; rejection would not itself prohibit infrastructure work funded from other sources.

question: E
title: Baltimore City Police Department
explanation: Whether to add Charter provisions establishing the Police Department as a city agency and defining the Police Commissioner's appointment, departmental authority, police duties, and police districts.
if_for: Adopt the proposed Charter framework for the department, commissioner, and officers.
if_against: Reject these proposed Charter provisions; the amendment would not be added to the Charter.

question: F
title: Inner Harbor Park
explanation: Whether to change the Inner Harbor Park Charter provision to allow multifamily housing and off-street parking within an expanded 4.5-acre area, alongside commercial uses, and exclude areas used for housing and parking from the public-park dedication.
if_for: Adopt the land-use changes and increase the relevant area from 3.2 to 4.5 acres. Approval is not evidence that redevelopment was completed.
if_against: Keep the existing Charter restriction instead of adopting these changes.

question: G
title: Community Reinvestment And Reparations Fund
explanation: Whether to create a continuing fund whose money would remain available across fiscal years and be used exclusively for eligible work of the Community Reinvestment and Reparations Commission.
if_for: Establish the fund and authorize city ordinances governing its oversight and administration. The question does not authorize a fixed dollar amount.
if_against: Do not establish this fund through the proposed Charter amendment.

question: H
title: Reducing The Size Of The City Council
explanation: Whether to reduce the number of City Council districts from 14 to 8 and require a mayoral redistricting plan after voter approval of a change in the number of districts.
if_for: Adopt the reduction to eight districts and the accompanying redistricting requirements.
if_against: Keep 14 districts and reject the accompanying Charter changes.
